German Bohemians ( German : Deutschböhmen und Deutschmährer ; Czech : čeští Němci a moravští Němci ), later known as Sudeten Germans ( German : Sudetendeutsche ; Czech : sudetští Němci ), are ethnic Germans living in the Czech lands of the Bohemian Crown , which later became an integral part of Czechoslovakia . Before 1945, over three million German Bohemians constituted [ 1 ] about 23% of the population of the whole country and about 29.5% of the population of Bohemia and Moravia. [ 2 ] Ethnic Germans migrated into the Kingdom of Bohemia , an electoral territory of the Holy Roman Empire , from the 11th century, mostly in the border regions of what was later called the " Sudetenland ", which was named after the Sudeten Mountains . [ 3 ]
